text: This is so true, that you may think you connect yourself with two friends to-day, and be obliged tomorrow to make your option between them as enemies; observe, therefore, such a degree of reserve with your friends as not to put yourself in their power, if they should become your enemies; and such a degree of moderation with your enemies, as not to make it impossible for them to become your friends.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXIX, to his son, London, August 21, Old Style 1749
